title: Move Python scripts that generate dissector data to their own subdirectory
description:
Start cleaning up the tools directory by moving the Python scripts that generate dissectors and/or dissector data to their own folder under tools/generate_dissectors.

Rename scripts that generate data outside of the dissector file to generate-\<dissector name\>-data.py
Rename scripts that generate data inside of the dissector file to generate-\<dissector name\>.py

Make updates as needed to ensure they still run after the move/rename

Python scripts directly involved the build (CMake files) got their own commit.

AI-Assisted: no

notes.body:
This is aimed at a standardization/cleanup process.
1. Should we have a consistent naming convention for the generators (like always using "generate" as a file prefix name)?  If so, that should probably be done now in this MR (just to get all of the "git renames" out of the way)
2. Yes, I would like to migrate/port the Perl scripts separately as time allows.
3. @geraldcombs - Is there pipeline/automatic script updates that need to be updated when this MR is approved?  I didn't see anything in the repo calling these scripts out by name.
4. Would have a separate MR to move the Python scripts that generate data for the epan directory

> Is there pipeline/automatic script updates that need to be updated when this MR is approved?

The weekly update job would have to be updated: gitlab.com/geraldcombs/update-ws-numbers/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml.

It might make sense to move some of the weekly update logic from the update-ws-numbers CI job to a master script under *tools* that runs the various update scripts, logs errors to a file (for the commit message), and prints a list of changed files (for `git add`). This would reduce some of the current brittleness; when someone adds or changes a generator it often takes a while to get everything to run correctly across each of our branches.
weekly_updates.py was a good idea and is updated as needed for this MR.

There was a deliberate effort to collect all tools in let's see, `\tools`. This is now being reversed and put forward in an MR. I would rather see a discussion first. That may be just me though.

I was just looking to organize things because I think the '\tools' folder is getting a bit unruly.  But I was also thinking about maybe have the dissector_generators as a subfolder to tools. To me it was more important to identify them than where they end up.
I think it makes more sense to keep everything under "tools". Moving the generators to their own subdirectory makes sense as well.

I originally liked spreading them out, but it started to get wonky with all of the different files being affected, so the latest version has everything in a subdirectory of tools.
I think I'll also standardize the naming convention (for the "git renames").
And also, since the weekly_update.py is now part of the repo, I think I'll tackle the /epan generated data as well.
Not inspired on where the scripts that generate /epan data should go, so skipping it as part of this MR.
